script: AddBarEvent orbiting_spoon_start "Visit 'The Orbiting Spoon' diner" "Tucked into the back of the concourse hums 'The Orbiting Spoon', a massive, jury-rigged Domain-era culinary fabricator. There are no VIP rooms here; captains, officers, and grease-stained deckhands all crowd into cracked vinyl booths to eat warm, real food from the clanking dispenser chutes."

text: An emergency klaxon chimes from the jury-rigged fabricator as your cred-chit comes up empty. The machine's ancient Domain operating core overrides local lockouts, and its auxiliary relief chute clunks open with a dense nutrient brick and a fuel chit under Domain Relief Protocol 44-B. Austere charity from a forgotten age.
options:

100:orbiting_spoon_leave:Take the supplies and return to the concourse

text: You walk past the bar counter to the corner housing 'The Orbiting Spoon'. Painted in regulation dull battleship gray with Hegemony Navy commissary seals, the jury-rigged Domain fabricator clunks rhythmically under the watchful eye of an armed commissary guard. Off-duty ratings eat at stamped steel benches in disciplined quiet under the smell of ozone, iron broth, and deck disinfectant.

The antique Domain fabricator shudders with a deep hydraulic clunk, venting ozone as its heavy brass dispenser tray slides out. A stamped metal platter holds a thick bowl of iron-rich soy stew, dense shipboard hardtack, and a scalding mug of chicory coffee. Austere, piping hot, and engineered to fuel a twelve-hour patrol burn.

You approach the acoustic-damped lounge where Tri-Tachyon has retrofitted the bar's Domain-era 'Orbiting Spoon'. Its antique casing has been gutted and replaced with sleek matte-carbon panels and biometric pay terminals, humming with clinical efficiency as corporate contractors dine at banquettes beneath the soft blue flicker of overhead stock tickers.

The modified Domain chassis hums at a high molecular frequency before unsealing its magnetic delivery hatch with a soft hiss of coolant vapor. A matte-black composite tray presents laser-seared synth-fillet beside an iridescent amino-gel matrix and chilled nootropic soda. Mathematically optimized to sharpen neural latency without gastrointestinal drag.

You find the bar's 'Orbiting Spoon' draped in crimson Lion's Guard pennants beneath glowing aquaculture display tanks of azure crustaceans. Diktat engineers have bolted high-pressure steam lines and external spice vaporizers to the Domain fabricator, while patrol captains converse over reef wine under the warm scent of clarified butter and charred peppers.

The brass-vented Domain machine roars like an orbital thruster as its steam pistons crack open. A polished platter emerges carrying split Volturnian lobster tail in fiery pepper butter, spiced aquaculture flatfish, and a carafe of purple reef wine. Rich, decadent, and a sharp reminder of the wealth the Lion's Guard bleeds to guard.

You duck into the quiet refectory alcove housing the bar's 'Orbiting Spoon'. The Church has solemnly decommissioned the machine's synthetic fabricator circuitry with holy lead seals, instead using its massive Domain-grade thermal induction core as a sanctified communal baking oven for real soil-grown loaves and stews.

Spacers watch with quiet reverence as the Church-consecrated Domain thermal unit unlatches its heavy insulated door. A fragrant ceramic bowl of barley and roasted fowl pie emerges alongside dense stone-ground sourdough, yellow churned butter, and steaming spiced cider. It tastes of fertile soil, woodsmoke, and honest labor.

You find the station's 'Orbiting Spoon' shoved into a rough subterranean bunker alcove. Cell fighters have hammered off every decorative panel, luxury circuit, and seasoning cartridge with heavy cold-chisels. Dented and scorched, the austere Domain machine simmers unspiced root broth over bare heating coils in the heavy silence.

The battered, chip-hammered Domain unit groans in protest, its uncalibrated chute sputtering grey penance broth into a dented tin mess kit beside boiled turnip mash and salted mutton. It is coarse, harsh, and completely unspiced: fuel meant only to keep a holy combatant alive and upright.

You step into a smoke-choked alcove cobbled together from scrap cargo hulls where the Pirates have chained the bar's Domain-era 'Orbiting Spoon'. Its warning lights are covered in black electrical tape, reeking of grease and sulfur while scarred corsairs slam dented tin mugs over games of high-stakes knuckle-dice.

Someone kicks the side of the junk-rigged Domain fabricator. It rattles violently, spits an acrid puff of grease smoke, and clangs open to dump sizzling blackened ribs, peppery fungal goulash, and a shot of caustic moonshine onto sheet metal. Fumes sting your eyes, but the heavy calories fuel a salvage run.

You find the bar's 'Orbiting Spoon' nestled behind colorful trade guild banners. League merchants have meticulously restored the Domain machine with engraved brass scrollwork and precision aroma-diffusers, its polished dispensing bays surrounded by ship captains and factors conversing over spiced olives and wine.

The polished Domain fabricator smoothly uncouples its pressurized amphora line with a chime, dispensing rosemary-rubbed lamb skewers, herbed flatbread, saffron waterfowl rice, and chilled citrus liqueur onto earthenware. Crisp, fragrant, and reflecting the flourishing trade routes of the League.

You step into a crowded alcove where an ancient, unpainted 'Orbiting Spoon' culinary fabricator rumbles in its Domain casing. Battered vinyl booths line the perimeter where tired independent haulers, freelance survey captains, and grease-stained mechanics hunch over steaming platters beneath flickering orange maintenance tubes.

The battered blue Domain fabricator hums reassuringly as its heavy dispensing hatch slides forward. A sturdy ceramic platter holds thick root-vegetable beef stew, golden waffles slathered in butter, and a mug of scalded black coffee. Honest, dependable spacer fare engineered to carry a crew through three consecutive hyperspace transitions.

$os_officerName cups their hot mug, exhaling slowly. "Vessel readiness nominal, Captain. Point-defense gunners ran interlocking screen drills on approach. Every fraction of a second counts when proximity alarms scream. Hot food without collision warnings... it's a rare gift. I'll keep our escort line intact if we don't overextend."

$os_officerName aligns their utensils, checking a datapad. "Drive readiness secure, Captain. Radiators recalibrated. Battles aren't won by reckless valor; controlling engagement envelopes and heat dissipation dictates the fight. An unforced breakdown is a tactical defeat. We stay disciplined, the ship stays intact."

$os_officerName leans back, weathered and calm. "Ship's in fighting trim, Captain. Maintenance clear, watches rested. Deep in the hyper-lanes, it's sound training and wardroom trust that hold the line. The crew expects steady nerves when shooting starts. We're ready for the next burn."

$os_officerName pushes their empty plate aside. "Good fuel, Captain, but idle warships corrode. We don't break their line by waiting; we pin their vanguard and punch through before escorts react. My gunners are dialed in. Put us up front and let us dictate the engagement tempo."

$os_officerName knocks back their drink, eyes glinting. "Savor it, Captain. Tomorrow isn't guaranteed. When shields flicker and armor buckles under heavy ordnance, victory belongs to whoever refuses to flinch. Give me a clear burn lane into their flank. Let's see which hull cracks first."

$os_officerName nods respectfully across the table. "Hot food and a quiet hour at the table go a long way out here, Captain. Weapons are calibrated, the bridge team is alert, and the ship is primed for combat deployment whenever you give the command."

$os_officerName glances at the overhead structural ribs, lowering their voice. "Defensive batteries at $marketName are heavy, Captain, but the approach corridor is congested. Sector politics are burning hot lately, and I don't trust half the transponders we've seen on the scope. If the Persean League or some pirate armada stages an in-system raid, civilian lighters will instantly choke the escape lanes. The Hegemony's inspections only make folks more jumpy. I've logged the firing arcs of their defensive platforms - if trouble starts, we keep our escorts tight against their point-defense envelope and burn hard for the nearest jump point."

$os_officerName meticulously reviews the patrol schedules on their cracked datapad. "Station security at $marketName maintains disciplined sensor sweeps, Captain, but their response flotilla follows predictable rotations. With the entire sector practically holding its breath for the next factional war, predictability gets you killed. Syndicate smugglers and Luddic pathers are already exploiting these exact blind spots across the Core Worlds. Furthermore, the gantry fuel lines here are severely aging. An unforced fire in the docking ring could trap our hulls during an emergency scramble. I have ordered our watch to keep cold thrusters pre-heated, just in case."

$os_officerName sips their bitter synthetic coffee, watching the crowded docking concourse with calm detachment. "A well-ordered station, Captain. Garrison patrols are disciplined, traffic control is professional, and the orbital defense grid provides solid overlapping fire. That's a rare comfort given the current state of sector affairs. With pirate warlords carving up the fringes and the major factions rattling sabers over AI core inspections, safe harbors are becoming desperately scarce. As long as our transponders stay green and we rigorously respect the local docking regulations, $marketName will remain a highly dependable staging harbor for our fleet."

$os_officerName smirks toward the bustling docking bay, leaning forward aggressively over empty plates. "Station batteries at $marketName pack punch, Captain, but their perimeter picket is stretched damn thin. The whole sector is getting soft, relying on outdated treaties and bloated patrols while independent operators bleed them dry. A fast strike vanguard from the fringes could slip past their blind sensor buoys and ruthlessly hit the berths before these local cruisers even clear their moorings. If the political situation finally snaps and we have to fight our way out of here, we seize the initiative and punch straight through."

$os_officerName chuckles darkly into their synth-ale glass, eyes tracking an armed patrol. "The local militia looks tough in their polished cuirasses, Captain, but they're sluggish. The whole sector is paralyzed by bureaucracy and cowardly admirals sitting safely on their homeworlds. Out here, action dictates reality. Their sensor grid has a massive blind spot right behind the primary solar array; I clocked it on our entry burn. If the political tension boils over or things go sour, we blow the docking clamps, gun the emergency thrusters, and let these shiny bastards try to catch our radioactive wake."

$os_officerName nods thoughtfully over their dented steel mug. "Defenses at $marketName appear adequate, Captain. Patrol craft are currently active and the station grid is fully powered. However, the wider sector is a powder keg right now. Tensions between the major blocs are bleeding into the independent systems, and supply chain disruptions mean pirate activity is spiking aggressively across all major hyperlanes. Trusting local security forces is a luxury we simply cannot afford anymore. It definitely pays to keep our watch heavily armed and our engines warm whenever we're docked anywhere near the fringe."
A deckhand leans in. "Docking at $marketName is house arrest, Skipper. ComSec checked ident-chits twice. Still, no one robs you. Salute the brass and keep moving."
An engine rating shakes their head. "Spotless station, Skipper, but $marketName charges for breathing. Sentry billed me five credits for gantry access. No one's signing their waivers."
A quartermaster snorts. "You can't walk ten meters here without Andrada's portrait glaring. The Lion's Guard acts like royalty, but fuel is cheap. Nod and fill the tanks."
A deckhand smiles quietly. "Peaceful here, Skipper. No flashing holo-ads. Smells like cedar and bread. Kept tech-scanners locked up so local deacons don't panic."
A deckhand glances nervously. "Every minute here feels like sitting on a live torpedo. Zealots eye our shuttle. Double watches posted. Let's eat and undock."
A marine taps the table. "Rough town, Skipper. Docking fees are whatever gangs squeeze before pulling iron. Ordnance is cheap, but watch your pockets. Don't drink glowing liquids."
A navigation rating chuckles. "The League loves a show. Merchants preach liberty while billing six dock fees. Promenade is lively, privateer gossip is worth it."
A hauler relaxes. "Real spacer territory, Skipper. No Hegemony patrols, no corporate lawyers, no zealots. Worn freighters and spare parts. Good place to catch our breath."
The crew grins proudly. "Looking over $marketName never gets old. Our colors, our gunners, no shakedowns. Built from our own salvage. We'll defend it to the last burn."
A senior rating sips coffee. "Every station has headaches, Skipper. But air is clean, clamps hold, galley's hot. Watches are posted; ready to burn on your word."
An engine rating taps hardtack. "Could fire this biscuit through a frigate's prow, Skipper! Stew is salty, chicory coffee wakes the dead. Beats shipboard algae paste."
A deckhand eyes their plate. "Weird corporate science, Skipper. Gristle-free steak and melting gel cubes, but that nootropic soda cleared my skull. Like stims without the flutter."
A gunner wipes their chin. "By the Lion, Skipper! Lobster was rich enough for a mutiny, skewers lit my tongue up. Reef wine beats the ship's recycler."
A cargo hand smiles. "Real soil-grown barley and fowl, Skipper. Ship food tastes of foil. Fresh bread and cider remind you why people live on planets."
A deckhand chews tough mutton. "Meat could patch a hull breach, Skipper. Broth lacks salt, but bitter tea hit my veins like stim-fluid. Keeps you moving under fire."
A mechanic laughs. "Charred ribs fall off the bone, Skipper, and goulash kicks. Moonshine stripped my teeth. Greasy, hazardous, and satisfying."
An astrogation mate clears their plate. "Saffron rice and duck beat the galley, Captain. Lamb flatbread herbs taste fresh, citrus drink clears the palate. We cleaned every tray."
A veteran hauler drinks coffee. "Honest frontier grub, Skipper. Beef stew, hot syrup, and black coffee strong enough to strip paint. Solid calories keep a spacer standing."
The crew raises mugs. "Skipper, harvest from our colony, cooked by our people... nothing beats it. Tastes like home, worth every burn."
A seasoned deckhand grins. "Captain, after weeks of recycled rations, hot grease and fresh coffee are a luxury. Cures bulkhead fever fast. The watch is thankful."
Deckhands keep their voices down. "Spacers say a Hegemony convoy went dark near the jump-point. High Command calls it drive failure, dockers think something caught them in the storm."
A tech-rating leans close. "Corporate reps lost contact with a phase coil lab past the rim. Quiet bounties for independent runners to get core logs. No questions asked."
The crew snickers. "Lion's Guard is sweating, Skipper. Andrada hasn't broadcast in months, syndicates fight over pipelines. If he drops, Askonia's a warzone."
A deckhand whispers. "Synod is uneasy, Skipper. Outer communes report strange lights, elders warn caravans off Path borders. Pious call it omens, spacers think stealth warships."
A deckhand murmurs. "Path is moving munitions to core hubs, prepping strikes. Telling believers to hoard fuel. If their strike packs show on sensors, don't linger."
A marine grins. "Heavy League transport lost containment near Magec. Three raider wolfpacks racing for the carcass. Fences dumping stolen torpedoes cheap."
A navigation rating sips their drink. "Kazeron's demanding defense tithes, claiming Hegemony aggression. Half the colonies refuse, hiring mercenaries instead. Privateer bounties are high, Captain."
A scavenger leans in. "Scrapper limped in with scorched radiators. Claims they found an ancient Domain signal in the rim. Prospectors are racing out there."
The crew grins. "Freight skippers are praising $marketName, Skipper. Lower tariffs and real security pulling trade from Core. Engineers were asking how to sign with us."
A deckhand traces a line. "Gantry chatter is nervous, Skipper. Haulers say automated contacts shadowed them past the fringe. Fringe is restless. Best keep point defense manned."
You leave the mess hall table, drop your meal chits at the commissary hatch, and step back out into the bustling concourse, refreshed and ready for the next burn into hyperspace.
You sit with off-duty watchstanders. Over hot food, veterans and rookies talk fuel margins and close calls. Exchanging advice on sensor alignment and micro-fractures steadies the crew.
